chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), regarding

two men killed a man deliberately, and for him were two guardians, so one of the guardians forgave. So he said: 'When one of the guardians forgives both of them, the killing would be staved off from them, and the wergild would be dropped from both of them by the measurement of the share of the one who forgave, and they would pay the remainder from their wealth to the one who did not forgive.' And he said: 'Forgiveness of every one with a share is allowed.'
ai.seo_question: How does the forgiveness of one guardian affect the qisas and diyah for multiple perpetrators in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of independent agency in qisas, establishing that each heir's forgiveness is distinct and does not require the consent of others. It highlights the Shia legal view that while one heir's pardon removes the death penalty for both perpetrators, the financial liability (diyah) remains partially enforceable against the unforgiving heir's share, reflecting the balance between mercy and justice in retributive law.
